problems.source_says: The length index averages standardized token, word, and sentence counts. These are text-length counts, not counts of ideas, categories, or unique ideas as category_count is defined in codebook Section 6. The elaboration construct is supported, but the measure code is not; the codebook supplies no explicit text-length-count category, so its replacement code is unresolved.
problems.quote: Length index averages the z-scores of tokens, words, and sentences.

problems.source_says: The Session Two outcome uses the same standardized token/word/sentence length index. It does not count ideas or idea categories, so category_count is unsupported under the codebook definition. Its elaboration construct, participant unit, and after_ai question remain supported; the replacement measure code is unresolved.

problems.source_says: The reported Table 6 estimates use a composite of the mean human grade and the AI grade. human_raters does not distinguish this mixed measure from the separately reported human-only measure. The form accurately discloses the mixture in measure_detail and notes, but its choice of a single human_raters code is an undocumented coding convention: Section 6 defines human raters and model judges separately and provides no mixed-rater code. The composite classification therefore remains unresolved, rather than being explicitly supported as a human-rater-only measure. Table A6 and Figure A4 distinguish the two grading sources.
problems.quote: For our main regressions, we use the average of human and AI grader scores for each dimension
problems.locator: PDF p. 13, Section 3.4; p. 40, Table 6 Panels A-B and notes; p. 66, Table A6 Panels A-B; p. 54, Figure A4; creativity-codebook.md Section 6, Measure (human_raters and automated_score).

form_value.notes: Separate records for all five immediate quality dimensions and both readability-index outcomes are omitted under the cap; immediate dimension coefficients are preserved in S1-O3 measure_detail.

problems.source_says: Two output-scored readability-index outcomes are omitted from the outcome array, as the form acknowledges under its 15-outcome cap. Table 5 reports Session One control mean 0.000, ITT 0.061 (SE 0.088), TOT 0.090 (SE 0.132), with printed N = 104 control and 210 total; Session Two control mean 0.000, ITT 0.065 (SE 0.103), TOT 0.097 (SE 0.153), with N = 99 control and 199 total. This ancillary writing-style family is relevant on the same basis as the retained lexical-diversity and length indices: it is computed on each produced essay, with question with_ai in Session One and after_ai in Session Two, construct other, and participant unit. Table A5 Panel B also reports its four component measures. This is an acknowledged coverage gap, not a transcription error; Table A5 prints the already-flagged alternative Session One N of 209.
problems.quote: Readability index averages four z-scored measures (sentence length, syllables per word, Flesch-Kincaid grade level, and Flesch Reading Ease), with signs oriented so that higher values indicate easier readability.
problems.locator: PDF p. 13, Section 3.4; p. 39, Table 5 Panel B, columns 1-6 and notes; p. 65, Table A5 Panel B; p. 32, Figure 6; form notes; creativity-codebook.md Sections 1 and 6.

The five immediate ITT coefficients and SEs preserved in S1-O3 measure_detail are accurate, but these outcomes lack separate records for their with_ai question, usefulness construct, participant unit, and mixed human/AI measure. This is partial coverage acknowledged by the form under its outcome cap, not an error in the preserved coefficients. The five delayed counterparts are separately recorded as S1-O11 through S1-O15.
